body:
Part of #36. Plan step **P03**. Builds on merged SQL-default startup #37; do not reimplement that change.

Blocked by: #38, #39. These are completion dependencies; synthetic groundwork exceptions are stated below.

## Outcome

A declared real SQL population reaches the existing local financial store with truthful provenance and only the capabilities supported by P02 (#39). A raw preview remains a raw preview. Preparation and any subsequently authorized isolated refresh reuse the same normalization and validation; dashboards remain offline SQLite readers.

## Work and acceptance

- [ ] Add a focused failing contract for real financial input and unsupported raw-preview rejection. Record actual behavior rather than treating a missing executable as an application failure.
- [ ] Implement the approved source mapping/package version with declared lineage, period/coverage, source cutoff, source/mapping identity and exact decimal/ID preservation. Do not relabel real data as synthetic or simply remove mapping guards.
- [ ] Integrate the validated mapping through existing normalization, package validation, staging and atomic activation. Retain named, validated IPC operations and protected credentials; no renderer SQL or public service.
- [ ] Start with one declared month plus required cost/return/conversion dependencies. Enforce measured row/byte bounds and honest partial coverage. Do not remove limits as a substitute for capacity evidence.
- [ ] Prove initial import, identical import, corrections/deletions, wrong lineage, malformed/unsupported inputs, cancellation and interrupted activation. Failures retain the last valid financial dataset and raw preview as applicable; all app-owned expenses, settings, adjustments, history and accepted reports survive.
- [ ] Verify the SQL-default flow can reach the validated report when supported and a truthful preview/unavailable state when unsupported. Do not promote every successful SQL connection to financial readiness.
- [ ] Preserve synthetic-package and prior saved-report compatibility. Add only the migration/version changes demanded by the approved contract and verify recovery round trips.

## Likely touch points

[src/source/sql-server.ts](https://github.com/AlesSystems/esmer-market-analytics/blob/6d717bef53f3a7fcf23bb9845e809ae9c79603a3/src/source/sql-server.ts), `src/source/sql-package.ts`, `src/source/package.ts`, `src/source/extract.ts`, `tools/prepare-sql-backup.ts`, `src/store/store.ts`, `src/service/worker.ts`, `src/reports/query.ts`. `src/source/live.ts` only if the already authorized isolated refresh must select the supported candidate path. Confirm actual flow before editing.

Extend existing `live-mapping`, `raw-report-readiness`, `analytics-package`, `import-activation`, `import-failures`, `store-ownership` and recovery integration tests. Do not duplicate the transport/store implementations.

## Exit gate

Independent source expectations reconcile with the normalized local population; rejected reads/imports preserve valid data. The packaged application imports and reopens the declared dataset offline. Applicable A01–A05 evidence is recorded; full history, Windows and production/live rollout remain separate gates.

## Execution and evidence

This is a planning backlog, not an instruction to start implementation. First settle the named decisions in P01 (#38) with the user. For each behavioral change, expose the missing contract with a focused failing test, record the actual failure, make the smallest implementation change, and run the relevant checks. Reuse the existing Vitest, Playwright packaged-desktop and synthetic SQL harness; do not create a new orchestration framework.

Use coherent Conventional Commits (`test:`, `feat:`/`fix:`, then evidence as needed). Record the task/gate, commit/build, opaque fixture/source batch, environment, command/procedure, expected and actual result, evidence location and remaining limits. Synthetic success is not source validation; macOS success is not Windows acceptance. Preserve unrelated work and accepted reports. Source access and production rollout retain their separate authorization boundaries.
title: [P1] Feed validated SQL profit data through the existing import pipeline
